title: Phase-field modeling of multi-flake growth and grain-boundary formation in CVD-grown 2D materials
content: Controlling domain morphology and grain-boundary formation is essential for tailoring the properties of two-dimensional (2D) materials grown by chemical vapor deposition (CVD). Here, we develop a three-field phase-field framework for the concurrent growth and impingement of multiple 2D flakes. The model couples a phase field delineating the flake, a surface adatom concentration field, and a continuous orientation field describing the crystallographic orientation of individual domains. By varying the effective adatom supply flux, surface diffusivity, and characteristic attachment timescale, we identify how competition between adatom transport and boundary attachment governs flake morphology. Lower diffusivity and faster attachment favor narrow, three-armed, star-like structures, whereas enhanced adatom redistribution or slower attachment promotes compact triangular domains. Increasing the adatom supply flux reduces the relative nonuniformity of the concentration field and produces rounded, compact morphologies. In multi-flake systems, overlapping adatom-depletion zones generate growth competition and modify the evolution of neighboring domains, while the orientation field resolves impingement and grain-boundary formation between misoriented flakes. Using the collision configurations of Artyukhov et al. as a benchmark, the model reproduces their bowtie-like bicrystals. Collision maps that vary the position and nucleation delay of a second flake show when an arrow-shaped rather than a bowtie bicrystal forms, and that a flake nucleating next to an edge of an earlier one, inside its adatom-depletion zone, reaches only about 40% of the area of the earlier flake, compared with 90% for independent growth. This computationally efficient continuum framework provides a qualitative mesoscale description relating kinetic growth parameters to domain morphology and polycrystalline microstructure.
